name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,668

clue.text: Put an end to child holding on to rubbish elephant's head

indicators.note: to hold something is to have it inside you, so 'child' wraps around what follows
the head of a word is its front, so only the opening letter of 'elephant' is used

blocks.note: a kid is a child
bosh is nonsense, rubbish
first letter of elephant

explanation.surface: A parent stops a child clutching a piece of junk shaped like an elephant's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On to' attaches the elephant's head after the rubbish, and both go inside the child before its final D. Bosh is a dated British word for nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: To put the kibosh on something is slang for stopping it dead, so kiboshed means halted or finished off.

indicators.note: a disease affecting a body changes it, so the malaria disturbs the letters beside it

blocks.note: twelve letters of fodder

explanation.surface: A warning that a tropical fever is reaching the United States via a predator.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 down is SECOND-IN-COMMAND; the American second-in-command is the Vice President, and Kamala Harris held that office from 2021 to 2025.
explanation.definitionFit: She served as Vice President of the United States, the country's official deputy to the President.

clue.text: Money which is tied up in poisons

indicators.note: the thing that is tied up is placed inside the word for poisons

blocks.note: banes are poisons, as in henbane and wolfsbane
a knot is what gets tied

explanation.surface: Someone's wealth is locked away in toxic assets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Which is tied up' is a descriptive phrase standing for a single noun, the thing you tie. Bane survives mainly in plant names like wolfsbane.
explanation.definitionFit: Banknotes are paper currency, the most familiar physical form of cash.

blocks.note: to second a motion is to back it
kept as it is
an order is a command

explanation.surface: A deputy is restored to good standing or put back in the queue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back in order' reads like one phrase meaning restored, but it splits into three words taken one by one.
explanation.definitionFit: A second-in-command is the officer ranking just below the leader, which is what a deputy does.

indicators.note: whatever changes is rearranged, so the letters before it move around

blocks.note: seven letters of fodder

explanation.surface: A film shoot wraps just as the set is being rebuilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wraps' looks like film jargon for finishing a shoot, which the scene change encourages; here it is the plain verb for covering something.
explanation.definitionFit: To encase something is to enclose it completely in a covering, the same as wrapping it up.

clue.text: Marginal damage to this girl's clothes

indicators.note: damaging something knocks it out of shape, so the letters it acts on get jumbled
clothes cover the outside of a body, so only the outer letters of 'girl' are wanted

blocks.note: used as it stands
the outside letters of girl

explanation.surface: A small tear or stain on a young woman's outfit, not worth fussing over.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pairs 'this girl's clothes', but 'clothes' acts on 'girl' alone while 'damage to' acts on THIS plus those outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something slight is small and of little importance, just as a marginal difference barely registers.

clue.text: Makeshift Italian side win against grand royal entourage

indicators.note: a makeshift arrangement is improvised, so the letters are thrown together in a new order

blocks.note: fourteen letters of fodder
G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A patched-together Italian football team beats a big name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Against' simply sets G alongside the rest of the fodder before the whole lot is shuffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladies-in-waiting are the noblewomen who attend a queen or princess, forming part of her household retinue.

definitions.note: reads as the phrase GO RED

blocks.note: pierced, as a bull's horn pierces a matador
22 across is ALARM, and a warning light may turn to the colour of danger

explanation.surface: A reassurance to someone stuck that help comes when the signal sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as GO RED: alarms and warning lamps sometimes do exactly that. Read whole, it is the past tense of gore.
explanation.definitionFit: Gored means stabbed with a horn or tusk, one violent sense of stuck; alarm lights flash red to warn.

blocks.note: a to-do is a commotion or fuss
with means together with, alongside

explanation.surface: A worry about the commotion happening right next to you.
explanation.walkthrough: A to-do is a British word for a fuss or palaver.
explanation.definitionFit: Something to do with a subject relates to it, the same meaning as the preposition concerning.

clue.text: A smaller group of alien vessels overhead

indicators.note: in a down entry, what is overhead is written above, so the vessels come before the alien

blocks.note: subs are submarines
ET, the film's extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: A handful of alien spacecraft hovering above.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overhead' only makes sense in a down light, where the vessels are written above the alien.
explanation.definitionFit: In mathematics a subset is a collection drawn from within a larger set, hence a smaller group.

blocks.note: to staff a desk is to man it
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A fixated boss running the workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' is a verb here, not the noun for employees.
explanation.definitionFit: Manic describes frenzied, driven behaviour, close in sense to obsessive energy or fixation.

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so the number receives the European

blocks.note: one hundred as the Roman numeral C, plus a second hundred written out
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Two hundred people took in a foreigner, then someone threw up.
explanation.walkthrough: 200 is built as C plus HUNDRED, one hundred each way. Chunder is Australian slang for vomit.
explanation.definitionFit: To chunder is Australian and British slang for vomiting, so chundered is past tense for having been sick.

clue.text: Catalogues keeping subset back for radicals

indicators.note: going back means reading from the end, so the number is turned around
to keep something is to hold it inside, so the catalogues surround the other piece

blocks.note: lists are catalogues
SUBSET is the answer to 9 down, so the word stands for its clue number

explanation.surface: Registers hide away a subgroup on behalf of extremists.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is that 'subset' is the grid answer at 9 down, so it stands for the number nine, which is then reversed and tucked in after the first letter of the catalogues.
explanation.definitionFit: Leninists are followers of Lenin's revolutionary communism, a classic example of political radicals.

blocks.note: a finale is the end
ow is what you say when something hurts

explanation.surface: A critic's verdict: the last act of the show was agony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's painful' is a whole phrase standing for the exclamation you would make.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow is to bestow money or a quality on someone, a more formal way of giving.

indicators.note: one thing sits inside the other, so the single letter goes into the constellation's word

blocks.note: a constellation is a group of stars, the question mark flagging the loose definition
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An airline naming its aircraft after star patterns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' pulls towards aircraft, and 'Constellation' was also a Lockheed airliner, but it means a flight of steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight is a set of steps between floors, and stairs are exactly that.

clue.text: Journey from home to get stoned

blocks.note: a trip is a journey
someone out is away from home

explanation.surface: Someone leaving the house for a day out that turns into a drugs binge.
explanation.walkthrough: The drug sense of trip links both halves, so the surface points at the answer while seeming to be about travel.
explanation.definitionFit: To trip out is slang for experiencing the effects of hallucinogenic drugs, much like getting high.

indicators.note: something that stores goods holds them inside, so the letters sit within the phrase

blocks.note: runs from the second O of snooper to the E of ivermectin

explanation.surface: A spy with a valid permit holds a stash of the anti-parasite drug ivermectin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snooper' is also a fair definition of the answer, a secret agent, but here it just supplies letters; the definition is 'Valid'.
explanation.definitionFit: A law or rule that is operative is in force and has effect, which is what valid means legally.

clue.text: Executive committee receives note about way of feeling as others do

indicators.note: whoever receives something takes it in, so the committee holds everything after it
about means around, so the note wraps round the way

blocks.note: the first letters of executive and committee
mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
a path is a way

explanation.surface: A board gets a memo about how to be more considerate.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest, one inside the other: 'receives' and 'about' each wrap what follows them.
explanation.definitionFit: An empathic person shares and understands the emotions of other people, sensing their moods from within.

clue.text: Bill Bailey show possibly calms mice you'd stimulated

indicators.note: something stimulated is stirred up, so these letters are agitated into a new order

blocks.note: thirteen letters of fodder

explanation.surface: A comedian's act soothes the very rodents that were earlier stirred up.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill Bailey is a British comedian whose stand-up is built around songs and instruments. 'Possibly' marks him as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: His stage shows mix jokes with piano and guitar numbers, a genre known for comic songs.

indicators.note: something said is spoken, so the word is judged by its sound, not its spelling

blocks.note: a deputy's boss is the person in charge

explanation.surface: A deputy reports the chief's favourite tunes.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 is SECOND-IN-COMMAND, whose boss is the leader; lieder, German for songs, is pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieder are German art songs for voice and piano, such as those of Schubert, so plural songs.

blocks.note: a loud South American primate named for its call
an embarrassing, glaring blunder

explanation.surface: An ape has committed a real blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is', linking two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Howler monkeys are named for their loud calls, and a howler is also a glaring error that invites laughter.

clue.text: Tool used to be written up by journalist

indicators.note: in a down entry, writing upwards reverses a word

blocks.note: a hack is a journalist, usually a jobbing one
was is the past of be

explanation.surface: A report by a reporter on a gadget that has gone out of use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Written up' sounds like reporting, the journalist's job, which hides its role as a reversal in a down light; 'by' just means next to.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacksaw is a fine-toothed handsaw in a frame, used for cutting metal.

clue.text: Signal in the style of the Marines

blocks.note: à la is French for in the style of
RM is the Royal Marines

explanation.surface: A bugle call or flag signal done the military way.
explanation.walkthrough: RM stands for the Royal Marines, Britain's naval infantry.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarm is a warning sound or signal that alerts people to danger.

indicators.note: 4 down is the word for wraps, so the phrase wraps around the letters wanted

blocks.note: runs from the second letter of baby's to the first of meal

explanation.surface: A baby's dinner is gobbled up greedily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gorge' wants to be the verb for overeating, which suits the baby's meal; it is the noun, a chasm. The indicator is the cross-reference 4, ENCASES.
explanation.definitionFit: Abysm is an old poetic form of abyss, a deep chasm like a ravine.

indicators.note: a deal that founders collapses, so its letters fall apart and regroup

blocks.note: nine letters of fodder

explanation.surface: A merger between restaurant chains falls through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Founders' could be read as the people who set up the chain; it is a verb meaning fails.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchilada is a Mexican dish of a rolled tortilla filled and baked in chilli sauce.

indicators.note: something that disintegrates breaks into bits, so the letters come apart and reform

blocks.note: nine letters of fodder

explanation.surface: Someone hammers the keys on a keyboard while a spiritual retreat falls apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punches key' reads as typing; 'Punches' is the plural noun and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A haymaker is a wild, swinging blow with the fist, so haymakers are hefty blows thrown in a fight.

clue.text: Here in Chamonix, the air finishes much colder

definitions.note: the answer means colder; 'much' adds emphasis

indicators.note: the finish of a word is its last letter, so only the endings of 'the' and 'air' count

blocks.note: ici is French for here, and Chamonix is a French ski resort
last letters of the and air

explanation.surface: A skier in the Alps notices the mountain air turning chillier at the end of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: Chamonix tells you to translate into French; 'finishes' takes the last letter of each of the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Icier is the comparative of icy, meaning more freezing and wintry in temperature.

indicators.note: the last word in the clue is told to go at the front of the answer

blocks.note: to twig is British slang for to understand
let's is short for let us, what we should do

explanation.surface: Snack time: first let's make sure everyone knows the plan.
explanation.walkthrough: Twiglets are a British snack of thin, knobbly, Marmite-flavoured wheat sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: Twiglets are sold in packets as savoury nibbles, a British party-food brand.
